literal: Ruin that is like prosperity, and death that becomes continued existence, are rare for any except the eminent.
translation: A ruin that yields prosperity and a death that becomes eternal living are impossible for any but the truly eminent.
modern: புகழைத் தரும் வறுமையும், என்றும் நிலைத்திருக்கும் தன்மையுடைய சாவும் அறிவுடைய மேலோர்க்கு அல்லாமல் மற்றவர்களுக்குக் கிடைப்பது அரிது.
explanation: The couplet explains how the eminent or wise (vittakar) transcend the physical limitations of loss and death through their fame. A loss or ruin (kēṭu) suffered by them in the path of virtue is actually like prosperity (nattam) because it enhances their glory. Similarly, their physical death (cākkāṭu) is not an end but becomes a form of eternal existence (uḷatākum) because their fame lives on forever. Such noble transformations of adversity and mortality are impossible for ordinary people and belong only to the truly accomplished.
